items.title: David Weinstein Interview, 1988-09-22
items.q: And the saxophone section was myself, Fazzola, Nina Piconi, uh, Leon Prima, Schalky, and, uh, Julian Lane with the brass section. Augie Chalang was on drums, Louis Macinta was on bass, Frank Pinero was on piano

ctx.x: Well, I hate to do that to you. I'm glad you did. I'm leading you. But I didn't want you to

contradict this. No. Well, I usually do anyhow. Okay. But, uh, I played out there, yes. And then, uh, uh, Leon and, uh, Schalker had both worked out there, but not together. They had each worked out there, I should say. And they had decided to go into business, so Hip Kinley, who had run a successful 25 cents club... No, I've got this backwards now. He opened the 25 club later? Let me think about that for a moment. But anyhow, the three of them invested enough money that they took over the Hollywood, and I don't…
Yeah. Did the, did the black bands also think of themselves as dance orchestras?
